Choose a name, select your preferred Cloud Service  Provider, as well as a Region and a Location. We now come into the Onboarding Page, which prompts  us to get started with a common service. Here you will find the Home Menu, Project Settings, and all the services currently available for you to use. The Header displays your current project  and organization. It allows you to switch between projects or create a new one. It also displays  your account balance. You will get five dollars when you create an account. There are also links  to our Slack Community of Builders, Notifications, links to our Documentation, and other account  controls. Starting on the left nav menu, let's go Home > Metrics. This is where you will be able to  see a detailed breakdown of usage statistics on a per service and per token basis. It can help you  understand which services are being used the most and where errors might be occurring. The activity  section will act as your admin console's audit trail. , Here you will be able to see any changes  to configurations, tokens created users invited, and more. You can click on any of these records to  see more detailed information as necessary. Next on the navigation menu you'll find 'Project Settings'  with a few subsections. On the 'General' tab you can rename your, project see from which location our  services are being served from, and project ID. Under 'Members', you can add new team members to  your project and assign them roles. A project admin has access to configure settings and create  tokens, while a project member can only use tokens and view configurations. On the 'Tokens' page, you  can see the tokens used to access Pangea APIs. They can be managed across your entire project  and updated to access different services. On the 'Branding' page, you can customize Pangea services  and components such as AuthN with your preferred icons, logos, and colors. The next area to explore is  'Services'. We currently have services in four core categories: Access, Compliance, Data Protection,  and Intelligence. Access services like AuthN make authentication easy and configurable with MFA,  email verification, and other features. Compliance services are all about making sure your data is  compliant, logging key events, and making sure you aren't storing PII or sensitive information data. Protection has services like key vault that handle key and secret management rotation and versioning.  Intelligence Services enable in-software decision making with security data sets including making  sure files, IP addresses, and other entities are not malicious. All services are laid out in a similar manner. It's important to note that some of  these services can be chained together to minimize the need for calls to multiple services while  satisfying complex use cases. An example would be chaining the Audit Log Service together with  the Redaction service using this toggle in the Audit Log Settings. This automatically removes  PII from any logged messages. When enabling a service, we can create a new token or extend an  existing token. Creating a new token would mean greater partitioning of access to the services, while extending a token with like services will make chaining those services easier. On token  selection, we will also be able to enable the services it has access to. Then we can try out the  service by making our first API call. Click on the 'Try it now' tab on the left menu. This will lead to  our interactive API reference documentation. Here we are going to log a secure phone number as  a string into the secure audit log. Heading back to the secure audit service logs, we can see the phone  number has been redacted. transcript: In this video, I'll show you how I  implement the GTD workflow in Notion. This is a 5 steps productivity  method from the book, Getting Things Done. Capture, process, organize, review, and engage.  The first step is capture. When we have a new idea, task, or project. The first step is to capture them. This helps free our brain for creative work and help us remember what we need to do. I  use the button blocks to help me quickly add a new task, project, or reference. this makes it  easy to click on even when I'm on my phone. The next step is process. We'll head over to our  inbox page and process our previously captured item. We first asked whether the capture task  is actionable. If it is a non-action item, you can eliminate it or save it as a reference by  dragging and dropping under the reference database. If it's actionable, but it takes less  than 2 minutes, do it now and check it off. If it takes longer than that, we then ask what is the next action? If there are maybe 1-2 steps  before, we can add sub-tasks below it. If there are multiple steps and that these tasks require an extended period of time to complete, it can be turned into a project by dragging and  dropping under the project database. Tasks can be organized into  projects, datelines, and context. If the task belongs to a project, we  can assign it to the respective project. And opening a project page, we'll be able to see  all the relevant tasks and add new ones from there. Once we process and organize the tasks, we can  mark it as a next action to remove it from the inbox view. Contexts can be a location, an action,  or an item. It can be anything that helps you batch similar tasks. If I need to buy eggs, I will  give you the grocery context and turn it into a next action. Similarly, for buy avocados, I will give  the same context and turn it into a next action. The next time I visit the grocery  store, I can filter for the contexts groceries to see everything I need to get from the store. The next step is review. A weekly review is what  keep your system free from chaos and keeping only what is relevant to you. Firstly, we want to get  clear. Think back on your past week, and see if there's anything you have missed. These items will  go into the inbox view and you can process them on the spot along with other items still in your  inbox. Secondly, we want to get current. We want to keep ourselves updated on the things that are  still on our next action list, or deadlines and events that are coming up. On top of that, we  also want to know the current projects that we are working on and the reference we have yet  to review. Lastly it's time to get creative. This is where we review our some dailies and decide if  there are any next action or projects we want to move forward. If we have any new and big ideas,  this is also the place and time to put it down. The final step in the GTD workflow is engage  No matter how organized you are, at the end of the day you need to do the work to get  things done. Use the respective pages as you go about your day, and start checking off  your tasks and move your projects forward.
